title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description:
Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of sizes `m` and `n` respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays as a floating-point value.

If the combined length `m + n` is odd, the median is the single middle element of the merged sorted array. If `m + n` is even, the median is the average of the two middle elements.

The overall run time complexity should be `O(log(m + n))`.
constraints: nums1 and nums2 are each sorted in non-decreasing order.
hints: Instead of merging both arrays in O(m + n), partition both arrays into a left half of size (m + n + 1) // 2 and a right half with the remaining elements.
Binary search the cut position i in the shorter array A (of length m <= n); the cut in B is determined as j = (m + n + 1) // 2 - i.
A partition is valid when A[i - 1] <= B[j] and B[j - 1] <= A[i] (treating out-of-bounds elements as -infinity or +infinity). Then compute the median from max(left) and min(right).

examples.explanation: Merged array is [1, 2, 3], so the median is 2.0.
Merged array is [1, 2, 3, 4], so the median is (2 + 3) / 2 = 2.5.
Merged array is [1], so the median is 1.0.
